subject: BrightCart - marketplace private offer & unit-price mapping (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Devon Shaw <devon.shaw@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart - marketplace private offer & unit-price mapping (post-call recap)

Hi Devon 

 great to talk earlier today. Quick recap and next steps on the marketplace private-offer path we discussed: 

1) What we heard from BrightCart on this call:
- You want to purchase via AWS Marketplace private offer (possible later on GCP/Azure).
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + search reranking (low-latency chat/summary endpoints).
- Current footprint: a mix of bursty real-time traffic and batch embedding jobs.

2) Info we need to finalize a private-offer unit price mapping (so marketplace PO can reflect the correct per-unit charge):
- Current and expected token volumes: monthly and peak (please provide 90/50/10 percentiles if you have them).
- Target budget range (monthly or annual) and target $/1M tokens you're aiming for on the marketplace listing.
- Which marketplaces to prioritize (AWS / GCP / Azure) and any internal procurement constraints (billing cadence, PO flow).

3) How we map Redwood pricing to a marketplace private offer:
- Marketplace listings often require a per-unit price (e.g., USD / 1M tokens) and we need to account for marketplace fees (AWS charges a fee that can vary by program).
- We'll produce a short mapping sheet (Redwood list price -> marketplace list price) with a few scenarios that hit your target $/1M after fees.

Next steps:
- Devon: can you confirm the monthly token volumes (current + expected 6-12mo ramp), and the target $/1M tokens you'd like the private offer to hit? 
- Rafael/Jonas: once we have volumes + target, we'll run a unit-economics mapping and propose recommended marketplace list prices for AWS/GCP/Azure (including estimates of marketplace fees and final effective $/1M tokens).

I've attached the quick meeting notes and will draft a mapping workbook once we get your numbers. Thanks 

 talk soon.

-- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

From: Devon Shaw <devon.shaw@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart - marketplace private offer & unit-price mapping (post-call recap)

Hi Marissa 

 thanks for the clear recap. Confirming details from our side below.

Token volumes (approx):
- Current baseline: ~200M tokens / month (combined inference + embeddings).
- Peak / expected ramp: we expect to ramp to ~800M tokens / month across the next 6-9 months as we onboard two additional product flows (search and personalized email generation).
- Typical burst: single-day spikes up to ~120M tokens.

Budget & target unit economics:
- Procurement has an initial target effective spend of ~$75k/month for inference (we have flexibility for expansion if unit economics are favorable).
- Target effective price (what we want to pay after marketplace fees): roughly $60-80 per 1M tokens. Ideally closer to $60 if possible.

Marketplace preference: AWS Marketplace private offer first. We may evaluate GCP/Azure later, but procurement prefers PO via AWS for now.

Other procurement notes:
- We will need the private offer to be represented as a single unit price line item per 1M tokens (or an equivalent per-100k token unit - we can handle either).
- Contracts team wants a simple mapping sheet showing Redwood's internal list price, marketplace list price, marketplace fee assumptions, and the final effective $/1M tokens.

Happy to jump on a short follow-up call with Rafael/Jonas if helpful - we can send our historical volume export if that helps with tiered pricing.

Thanks,
Devon
Devon Shaw
Head of Procurement | BrightCart
devon.shaw@brightcart.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart - marketplace private offer & unit-price mapping (post-call recap)

Thanks - digging in quick. Couple notes and a recommended mapping (high-level):

Assumptions:
- Redwood internal hosted list price (baseline for this exercise): $50 per 1M tokens (example reference).
- AWS Marketplace fee assumption: 12% (use conservative 15% in sensitivity).
- We'll map to a marketplace listing price that yields the target effective price after fees.

Scenario A - conservative (target effective $80 / 1M):
- Required marketplace list price = effective / (1 - fee) -> $80 / 0.88 ~ $90.91 -> round to $91 / 1M tokens.
- If Redwood's internal list is $50, margin to Redwood = $91 - (platform pass-through adjustments) -> we'll confirm internal reconciliation.

Scenario B - aggressive (target effective $60 / 1M at ramp volumes):
- Required marketplace list price = $60 / 0.88 ~ $68.18 -> round to $68 / 1M tokens.
- To support lower effective price we'd subsidize the difference from Redwood discounts or committed reserved capacity margins.

Marketplace listing unit recommendation: list per 100k tokens with price rounded appropriately to avoid very small decimals in AWS console. Example: for $68 / 1M -> $6.8 / 100k (we'd list $6.80).

Deliverables:
- I'll update the attached workbook with rows for AWS/GCP/Azure (using AWS fee 12%, GCP 10%, Azure 13% as starting points) and produce both scenarios (current volumes and ramp volumes).
- Jonas: confirm technical note on billing granularity (tokenization and rounding).
- Marissa: once workbook is ready we can share to Devon and set a short call with procurement if they want the usage export included.

I'll shoot the updated mapping back by EOD.

-- Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
